title: Diary Template for Kids (Free Printable, KS1 and KS2)
description: A free diary template for kids ages 5 to 10. Big, friendly boxes for feelings, the best part of the day and tomorrow. Fill in, print or save as PDF.
h1: Diary template for kids: free and printable
intro: This free diary template for kids has big, simple boxes that children ages 5 to 10 can fill in: how I felt today, the best part of my day, something I learned and what I want to do tomorrow. Fill it in on screen, or print it blank for writing and drawing by hand. It works well for KS1 and KS2 diary writing too.

fields.label: The best part of my day
I am thankful for
fields.hint: A person, a pet, a snack...

sections.h2: What is on this kids diary page

blocks.p: Each box asks one easy question. Young children can answer with one word or a picture. Older children can write full sentences.

ul: **Today I felt.** Naming a feeling helps kids understand it.
**The best part of my day.** Every day has one, even a rainy one.
**Something tricky today.** A safe place to say what was hard.
**I learned.** Something from school, home or the park.
**I am thankful for.** A small habit of noticing good things.
**Tomorrow I want to.** Something to look forward to.

sections.h2: How to use the diary template with kids

steps.name: Print a few blank pages
steps.text: Press Print or save as PDF. Printing blank lets children write and draw by hand.

steps.name: Pick a cozy time
steps.text: After dinner or just before bed works well. Five to ten minutes is enough.

steps.name: Write the date together
steps.text: Younger children can copy it from a calendar. It is good practice.

steps.name: Talk first, then write
steps.text: Ask the questions out loud. For ages 5 and 6, an adult can write while the child talks, then the child adds a drawing.

steps.name: Draw in the margins
steps.text: A picture of the best part of the day counts as writing for little ones.

steps.name: Keep the pages together
steps.text: Put them in a folder or binder. Kids love reading old pages.

blocks.tip: A diary should feel safe. Ask before reading your child's diary, and thank them when they share it with you.

sections.h2: A filled in kids diary example

example.label: My diary
example.title: My diary
example.text:
Today I felt: happy and a bit tired.
Best part: we found a frog in the school pond!
Something tricky: I lost my water bottle.
I learned: frogs can breathe through their skin.
I am thankful for: Mrs. Patel who found my bottle.
Tomorrow I want to: go to the park with Dad.

blocks.p: For a younger child, the same page might just say "happy", "frog", "bottle", with a big drawing of a frog. Both are great.
In KS1, children start writing simple recounts of things that happened to them. A diary is a perfect way to practice.

ul: Use the template as it is, with one word or short sentence answers.
Practice the date, capital letters and full stops in each box.
Use time words out loud first: first, next, then, last.
Let children draw first and write a caption under the picture.
Good topics: a trip to the park, a birthday, a lost tooth, a new pet.

blocks.p: Our [diary for kids](/diary-for-kids/) page has more ideas for young writers.
In KS2, children write longer diary entries, often as a character from a story or history. They use the same parts every time.

head: Part
What to write
Example
rows: What a day I have had!
Events in order, past tense, first person

ul: Write as "I" (first person).
Use the past tense for what happened today.
Show feelings with details, like a pounding heart or shaky hands.
Use time words like meanwhile, eventually and the next morning.

blocks.p: Try a topic like [my first day at school](/diary-entry-about-first-day-at-school/) or [a rainy day](/diary-entry-about-rainy-day/). For step by step help, see [how to write a diary entry](/how-to-write-a-diary-entry/).

sections.h2: Ideas for what kids can write about

ul: The funniest thing that happened today
A game I played and who won
What I had for lunch and if I liked it
Something kind someone did for me
Something kind I did for someone
A dream I had last night
My favorite toy and why
If I could have any pet, it would be...
The best day I ever had
What I want to be when I grow up

blocks.p: There are many more in our [journal prompts for kids](/journal-prompts-for-kids/).

faq.q: Is this kids diary template free?
faq.a: Yes. You can fill it in on screen, print it or save it as a PDF for free. No sign up is needed. Anything typed is saved only in the browser on this device.

faq.q: What age is this diary template for?
faq.a: It is made for children ages 5 to 10. Younger children can answer with one word and a drawing, with an adult helping to write. Older children can write full sentences in each box.

faq.q: What should a child write in a diary?
faq.a: How they felt, the best part of the day, something tricky, something they learned and what they want to do tomorrow. Funny moments, games, food, friends and pets are all great topics.

faq.q: What are the features of a diary entry for KS2?
faq.a: A date, a greeting like Dear diary, events in time order, written in the first person and past tense, with feelings and thoughts, time words, and an ending that looks ahead. Many teachers also ask for an informal, chatty tone.

faq.q: How do I get my child to keep a diary?
faq.a: Keep it short and fun. Pick a regular time like bedtime, let them draw, and talk about the day before they write. Never correct spelling in their private diary. Praise them for writing anything at all.
